findings.title: Incomplete src rewrite
findings.body: The raw-HTML rewrite regex only matches double-quoted `src="..."` attributes. Single-quoted (``) or unquoted (``) sources are never rewritten. As a result: - Valid local images resolve relative to the temp HTML file and get a 403, so they don't render even with the setting on. - Blocked remote images in these forms never call `imagesBlockedCallBack`, so no info bar appears. Raw HTML passes through Markdig verbatim, so these forms are common in real documents. Consider handling all three quoting styles, or parsing the attribute properly.

findings.title: Blocking UI I/O
findings.body: `File.Exists` and `File.ReadAllBytes` run synchronously inside the `WebResourceRequested` handler, which executes on the UI thread. This handler is the path used for UNC shares, so a slow or unreachable share, or several large images, will freeze the preview pane and Explorer's host until each read completes. Consider using `e.GetDeferral()` and reading the file asynchronously, or returning a `FileStream` instead of buffering the whole file.

findings.title: Base path widening
findings.body:
The share-root calculation treats any directory starting with `\\` as `\\server\share`, which breaks for extended-length or device paths:
- `\\?\C:\docs` yields `\\?\C:`, which allows the whole drive.
- `\\?\UNC\server\share\...` yields `\\?\UNC`, which allows every server.
Either case would let a document load images far outside its folder or share. It is uncertain whether Explorer ever passes such paths to the preview handler, but explicitly detecting the `\\?\` and `\\.\` prefixes (or falling back to the document directory) would avoid this.

findings.title: Security concerns
findings.body: Path containment weakening (uncertain): the UNC share-root detection in `MarkdownPreviewHandlerControl` does not account for `\\?\` or `\\.\` prefixed paths. If such a path is supplied, the allowed base path becomes an entire drive (`\\?\C:`) or all UNC servers (`\\?\UNC`). Images from outside the intended folder or share would then be readable and rendered in the preview. Remote exfiltration is still prevented by the 403 block and disabled scripts.
